h1: Sima Thani Hotel — The Long-Running 5-Star Hotel in Central Korat That the Whole City Knows
intro: Mention a hotel in Korat and one of the first names locals think of is Sima Thani Hotel — a long-running 5-star hotel on Mittraphap Road that has been part of the city since 1990 and has long been the venue for the city's weddings, seminars and big banquets · What guests remember most is the soaring classic-style lobby, the spacious rooms, and the well-known Chinese restaurant and buffet · A major 2019 renovation gave the rooms a fresher look, and there's an outdoor pool, fitness, and spa massage · The central location is near the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo) and Terminal 21 Korat · From about THB 1,100/night, which is genuinely affordable for a hotel of this level

body.html: Overview and who it suits — The shortest way to put it: Sima Thani Hotel is literally "Korat's hometown hotel" · It's a 5-star hotel that has been open since 1990, part of Nakhon Ratchasima for more than thirty years, and a name nearly every local knows, because it has always been the venue for the city's weddings, class reunions, government seminars and big conferences · What sets it apart from the newer hotels in town is its "landmark" quality — a large building, a dignified soaring classic-style lobby, and the kind of generous common areas you find in older hotels but rarely in modern boutique places · From real reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the people most impressed here tend to be those in town for government or business work, families staying on after a wedding or banquet, people who prefer a spacious classic-feeling hotel over minimalist design, and travelers using Korat as a stopover before Khao Yai or Phimai Historical Park · Those who feel lukewarm are the ones hunting for a brand-new, modern, photogenic hotel, because even after the 2019 renovation the structure and overall feel are still those of an older hotel that emphasizes stateliness and usable space rather than trendy modern style · The hotel is still open and operating normally, holds an overall score of around 8.4 on Trip.com, and TripAdvisor ranks it among the top hotels in Nakhon Ratchasima — a sign that standards remain steady and a lot of people come back, especially locals

Location and getting around — The hotel sits on Mittraphap Road in the heart of Nakhon Ratchasima, the main artery of the city and of the lower Isan region · What makes this location an advantage is how conveniently it connects in every direction — it's close to the inner city, and going out to other districts or up Mittraphap Road toward Khao Yai/Pak Chong is a straight shot · It's only about a 4 min drive from Terminal 21 Korat and about 7 min from Save One market, a popular late-night food spot in Korat · The Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo), the heart of the city, is a few minutes' drive away, and The Mall Nakhon Ratchasima isn't far either · For those arriving by train, Nakhon Ratchasima railway station is about 4 km away with easy onward rides · Near the hotel there are also temples and small spots like Arts of Korat within walking distance · The honest note is that the hotel is right on Mittraphap Road, which is busy, especially during rush hour — if you're driving yourself, allow extra time in the evening · The good news is some reviews mention the rooms are fairly well soundproofed, so traffic noise from the main road rarely disturbs your sleep · Overall this location suits people with a car or easy access to ride-hailing more than those who want to stroll around a tourist district, because the strength here is being a central hub from which everything is easy to reach

"The lobby is beautiful and grand, with a soaring ceiling — dignified, just as you'd expect from the city's long-running hotel · The room is very spacious, the bed comfortable, and the staff are friendly and attentive. The breakfast buffet is tasty with plenty of choices."

Room types and decor — Sima Thani Hotel has 265 rooms in total, split across several tiers from standard rooms up to large suites · It starts with the Superior Room, the entry-level room, with a choice of two single beds or one large bed · Stepping up is the Deluxe Room at around 32 sqm with a King bed, the tier most people book because of the value, and there are also Grand Superior and Grand Deluxe rooms that are more spacious · For those wanting more room there are Studio, Junior Suite, Executive Suite, Premier Suite and Royal Suite, scaling up to large suites for important events or big families · The point reviews most often agree on in praise is that the rooms are very spacious for the price — an older-style room scale that gives more space than newer hotels · The beds are comfortable, the air-con cools thoroughly, the bathrooms have both a bathtub and a shower, and there's a minibar, safe, bathrobes and slippers · After the 2019 renovation, many parts of the rooms look clearly fresher · The honest note that comes up is that some rooms or corners of the building still show the hotel's age, such as carpet in some common areas starting to look worn, and the overall decor leans classic rather than modern · Anyone who wants the freshest room should request a renovated section when booking · But in terms of "room space for the price," Sima Thani clearly gives more than comparable hotels in Korat

Facilities and the pool — As a long-running 5-star hotel that positions itself as the city's event venue, Sima Thani offers a fairly full set of facilities · There's an outdoor pool on the terrace level that reviews describe as clean with a quiet, calm atmosphere, good for a morning swim or a relaxing soak · There's a fitness room with fairly complete equipment, a sauna, and a steam room for those wanting to unwind after a full day of travel · Another highlight is the spa and massage service — Thai massage, oil massage, and facial/body treatment courses, a service a hotel of this level does well · For seminars and banquets, Sima Thani has several large meeting and banquet rooms that handle anything from small group meetings to weddings and seminars for hundreds of people, the original strength that keeps locals thinking of this hotel · There's free parking with plenty of space, very important for people driving themselves or renting a car for Khao Yai, plus free Wi-Fi throughout · The note reviews raise is that the pool has no bar or poolside drink service, so it's a pool for swimming and quiet relaxation rather than a party-atmosphere pool bar — anyone expecting a resort-style pool with drinks should adjust their expectations here

Food and restaurants — Food is a clear strength of Sima Thani and a reason locals come even when they're not staying over · The hotel has several restaurants · The star most talked about is the Tapestry Chinese restaurant, known for dim sum, Cantonese cuisine, and Chinese banquet tables, which gets very high review scores and is popular with Korat locals for family meals · Another is The Grill Room, focusing on steak and Western food with a formal atmosphere, good for a special meal · Breakfast and the daily buffet are at Nai-Ruen restaurant, serving international food — Thai, Asian and Western · Many reviews praise the breakfast buffet as varied with good flavors, the part many say helps them start the day well · The hotel also has lunch/dinner buffets at certain times for around 490 baht per person, which a lot of locals come for · Beyond the hotel, the central location helps a lot, because nearby there are well-known Korat restaurants serving dishes like pad mee Korat, Isan eateries, and plenty of late-night food at Save One market to choose from · Overall the food here is something you can genuinely "come to eat" for, not just an add-on in the room package

Service and staff — Service is another point that earns consistent praise in real reviews, and a category that scores especially high · Many guests describe the same thing: the staff are friendly, smiling and attentive, from check-in to check-out · Being a long-running hotel with a team that has worked there for years gives the service a steady, professional feel, especially handling big events like weddings or seminars that require coordinating many parts at once · Small things like helping with luggage, recommending restaurants in town, or helping call a ride are mentioned positively often · When a problem comes up in the room, such as the air-con or equipment needing help, the team follows up and fixes it fairly quickly · To be straight, a few voices say that when the hotel has a big event and lots of guests, responses can be slower at times, but this is a minority note against the overall praise · This is an original strength that keeps Sima Thani in the hearts of locals and returning travelers

What real reviews say (both praise and gripes) — Pulling together opinions from Trip.com, Booking.com and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the beautiful, dignified soaring lobby that many photograph, very spacious rooms for the price, comfortable beds and good soundproofing despite being on a main road, a varied breakfast buffet, the very highly rated Tapestry Chinese restaurant, friendly staff with good service, spacious free parking, and value for a hotel of this level · On the note side: the most-mentioned point is decor and the building looking aged — even after the 2019 renovation, some corners are still older-hotel style, and carpet or some items in common areas are starting to look worn · Next is that the pool has no bar or poolside drink service, and the hotel sits on busy Mittraphap Road (though in-room noise is low thanks to good soundproofing) · Some also say that, while central, the location isn't a district you can stroll around — you need a car or ride-hailing · Most of these gripes are about "style and the hotel's age" rather than quality problems, and are solved by setting the right expectations — those who like dignified classic style will see it as charm, while those who like new and trendy may see it as a downside

"Came for a seminar at the hotel and stayed over — the room was bigger than expected at this price · The Tapestry Chinese restaurant is excellent, you can order dim sum for lunch · The hotel itself looks a little aged but it's clean, and all the staff are lovely. Great value for a 5-star."

Price comparison and value — The starting price for a Superior Room is about THB 1,100–1,300/night in the normal range · Stepping up to a 32 sqm Deluxe Room runs about THB 1,500–1,800, Grand Deluxe and Studio about THB 2,000–2,500, and Junior/Executive Suite-level suites about THB 3,000 and up, while the Royal Suite for special events costs more · All these prices can climb during long holidays, when there's an event in town, or in Khao Yai's tourist season, so it's worth comparing several platforms before booking · Compared with similarly ranked city hotels like Centara Korat starting around THB 1,600 or Kantary Hotel Korat starting around THB 2,100, what makes Sima Thani good value is that you get a 5-star hotel with spacious rooms, a dignified lobby, full facilities, and well-known restaurants at a lower starting price · What you trade is the newness of the building — if you can accept an aged classic style, Sima Thani delivers value in space, service and food that's hard to find at this price · But if your budget is the same and you weight the freshest rooms and modern design most, a newer hotel in town may suit you better

Good to know before booking — A rundown of what to check before booking Sima Thani · One — request a renovated section if you weight room freshness, because the hotel has both the 2019-renovated parts and parts kept in their original state; you can note the request at booking or check-in · Two — if you come when the hotel has a wedding or big seminar, the common areas can be livelier and busier than usual; anyone wanting quiet should check with the hotel first, or request a floor away from the banquet rooms · Three — the pool has no poolside bar, better for swimming and quiet relaxation than partying · Four — the hotel is on Mittraphap Road, so if you're driving allow extra time in the busy evening, but the good news is there's spacious free parking and good soundproofing · Five — some packages charge extra for breakfast, so check at booking whether the price includes breakfast, and if you come as a family, booking the buffet at Nai-Ruen included is often better value · Six — don't forget that the Tapestry Chinese restaurant is open to outside diners, so if you like dim sum, try a meal there

The bottom line — Sima Thani Hotel is a well-rounded central choice for people coming for business, a seminar/wedding, or a stopover before Khao Yai/Phimai, especially those who like a spacious hotel with a dignified classic feel and who weight food and service · Its strengths are its landmark status in the city, a beautiful lobby, spacious rooms, full facilities, the well-known Chinese restaurant and buffet, and an affordable starting price for a 5-star · What to understand is that this is a long-running hotel with a classic feel, not a brand-new boutique with trendy design — if you see the age as charm, it's great value, but if you're hunting for the freshest rooms or a resort atmosphere close to nature, you may want to look at other options · For the brief of "an affordable, reliable 5-star hotel in central Korat," Sima Thani still does it well and lives up to its long history in the city

faqTitle: Frequently Asked Questions — Sima Thani Hotel, Nakhon Ratchasima

faq.q: Where is Sima Thani Hotel · what's nearby?
faq.a: It's located on Mittraphap Road in the heart of Nakhon Ratchasima (Korat) · about a 4 min drive from Terminal 21 Korat · Save One market about 7 min · the Thao Suranari Monument (Ya Mo) about 10 min · Nakhon Ratchasima railway station about 4 km · on Mittraphap Road, with easy access out to Khao Yai or Phimai

faq.q: What's the starting price at Sima Thani Hotel · what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 1,100/night for a Superior Room · 32 sqm Deluxe Room about THB 1,600 · Grand Deluxe/Studio about THB 2,200 · Junior/Executive Suite about THB 3,200 and up · prices shift by season and holidays, so always compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Is Sima Thani Hotel old · what are the rooms like?
faq.a: The hotel opened in 1990 and had a major renovation in 2019 · it's a long-running hotel in the city with a classic feel and a dignified soaring lobby · rooms are very spacious for the price, beds are comfortable, and soundproofing is good · some corners are still older-style, so if you weight freshness, request a renovated section when booking

faq.q: Does Sima Thani Hotel have a pool and restaurants?
faq.a: Yes — an outdoor pool on the terrace level with clean water and a quiet atmosphere (no poolside bar), plus fitness, sauna and spa massage · there are 3 restaurants, including the Tapestry Chinese restaurant known for dim sum, The Grill Room steakhouse, and the Nai-Ruen international buffet

faq.q: Who does Sima Thani Hotel suit most?
faq.a: It suits people coming for business, a seminar/wedding, or a central stopover before Khao Yai/Phimai very well, and those who like a spacious hotel with a dignified classic feel and who weight food and service · it's less suited to people hunting for a brand-new boutique with modern design or a nature-resort atmosphere

faq.q: Is there parking here · is it noisy from the main road?
faq.a: Yes — spacious free parking, handy for people driving themselves or renting a car for Khao Yai · the hotel is on Mittraphap Road, which is busy in the evening, but the rooms are fairly well soundproofed, with reviews confirming traffic noise rarely disturbs sleep · if you're worried about noise, request a room not facing the road at check-in
